mathgap.title: Initial counts from 'has' statements
mathgap.principle: Treat statements of the form 'X has N potatoes' as the initial count before any transfers; they are not final values.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a problem contains both 'has' statements and transfer statements.
mathgap.example: Assuming 'Tina has 22 potatoes' is her final amount after receiving potatoes, which creates an inconsistency with the transfer.

mathgap.title: Apply transfers correctly
mathgap.principle: For each 'X gives K potatoes to Y' statement, subtract K from X's current count and add K to Y's count after the initial amounts have been set.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a problem includes any 'gives' statements.
mathgap.example: Ignoring the effect of 'Britt gives 15 potatoes to Tina' and leaving Britt's count unchanged.

mathgap.title: Direct comparison 'has K more than'
mathgap.principle: Interpret 'X has K more potatoes than Y' as the directed equation X = Y + K.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement explicitly says one person has a fixed amount more than another.
mathgap.example: Writing Reta = Jonathan - 9 instead of Reta = Jonathan + 9.

mathgap.title: Absolute difference for 'difference between'
mathgap.principle: Treat 'the difference between the number of potatoes that A and B have' as the absolute value |A − B|, not a directed subtraction.
mathgap.when_to_apply: In any statement that mentions a 'difference between' without specifying order.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'difference between the number of potatoes that C and D have' as C − D, leading to sign errors.

mathgap.title: Magnitude interpretation for 'has more than' in equality statements
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'The number of potatoes that X has more than Y is equal to the difference between ...', interpret it as X − Y = |C − D|, even if a prior fact indicates Y > X.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a difference‑equality uses 'has more than' but the known ordering contradicts the phrasing.
mathgap.example: Using Jonathan − Reta = Norene − Michelle despite Reta > Jonathan, instead of using |Jonathan − Reta| = |Norene − Michelle|.

mathgap.title: Propagate known absolute differences
mathgap.principle: When a statement fixes an absolute difference (e.g., 'has 9 more than'), propagate that as a fixed |A − B| = 9 to all related constraints.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a problem includes a fixed difference like 'has 9 more' and other constraints involve absolute differences.
mathgap.example: Failing to use Reta − Jonathan = 9 to deduce |Norene − Michelle| = 9, leaving the system under‑constrained.

mathgap.title: Symbolic substitution over guessing
mathgap.principle: Set up equations for all variables and solve them algebraically; avoid guessing values before the system is fully expressed.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When multiple unknowns appear and the problem forms a linear system of constraints.
mathgap.example: Randomly picking Norene = 25 without using the equations, which can violate other statements.

mathgap.title: Final consistency check
mathgap.principle: After obtaining a solution, verify that every original statement (including direction of inequalities) holds with the derived numbers.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Immediately before outputting the answer, once all equations have been solved.
mathgap.example: Accepting a solution that satisfies most equations but violates 'Reta has 9 more potatoes than Jonathan'.

mathgap.title: Use integer bounds to prune solutions
mathgap.principle: All counts are small non‑negative integers (typically 10‑30); discard any solution that falls outside this range.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When solving yields multiple integer possibilities for a variable.
mathgap.example: Obtaining a negative count for a person and still proceeding with that value.

mathgap.description: Treating 'has' statements as final counts after transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes the listed amounts already include the effects of later transfers, ignoring that transfers modify the numbers.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret 'X has N' as the initial amount before any 'gives' actions are applied.

mathgap.description: Interpreting 'has K more than' as X = Y - K
mathgap.why_it_happens: A sign reversal occurs because the phrase 'more than' is misunderstood as subtraction rather than addition.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Remember that 'X has K more than Y' means X = Y + K.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes order matters in the phrase, whereas the wording denotes an absolute difference.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always use the absolute value |A − B| for 'difference between' unless a direction is explicitly given.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the effect of transfer statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model does not update the giver's and receiver's counts, treating transfers as irrelevant to the final totals.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each 'X gives K to Y' by subtracting K from X and adding K to Y after establishing initial amounts.

mathgap.description: Not checking all constraints after solving
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model stops once a plausible value for the target variable is found, without verifying every original statement.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Perform a final verification that each statement (including inequalities and absolute differences) is satisfied by the solution.
